definitions.explanation: A Buddhist temple, used with the polite prefix お. The standard everyday form when referring to temples in conversation.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}にはお{寺|てら}がたくさんある。
examples.english: There are many temples in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}でお{寺|てら}にお{参|まい}りした。
examples.english: I visited a temple with my family.

examples.japanese: あのお{寺|てら}は{桜|さくら}の{名所|めいしょ}として{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: That temple is famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot.

notes:
The polite form of {寺|てら}, using the honorific prefix お. In everyday conversation, お{寺|てら} is much more common than the plain form {寺|てら}. The お prefix is not strictly honorific here — it has become a natural part of the word in spoken Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{寺|てら}に{行|い}く: to go to a temple
- お{寺|てら}にお{参|まい}りする: to visit a temple (for worship)
- お{寺|てら}を{回|まわ}る: to visit several temples
- お{寺|てら}の{鐘|かね}: a temple bell

TEMPLE VS. SHRINE:
- お{寺|てら}: Buddhist temple — features a {本堂|ほんどう} (main hall), {仏像|ぶつぞう} (Buddha statues), and often a {墓地|ぼち} (cemetery)
- {神社|じんじゃ}: Shinto shrine — features a {鳥居|とりい} (torii gate) and {狛犬|こまいぬ} (guardian lion-dogs)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寺院|じいん}: temple — a more formal, written-style word for Buddhist temples
- {寺|てら}: temple — the plain form, used mainly in compounds and written contexts
